justifications.c1: No UK figure for a chemical run-out closure; the only totals are planned multi-day closures (Whiterock £6,800, Valley £4,290) and an Australian $17k/day, plus qualitative lesson refunds, so the per-incident loss for a one-morning delay is unquantified.
justifications.c2: The file found no UK closure caused by a drum or IBC running dry; related closures (Southampton overnight dosing error, search-confirmed; Selkirk low chlorine; 2022 national shortage) exist but no run-out rate, and the daily plant-room check is only from one job advert.
justifications.c3: Visual stock checks on plant-room rounds, weekly multi-site inspections, bulk tanks with daily deliveries, and stock transfers during the shortage are documented, but with no labour time or cost.
justifications.c4: PWTAG Code of Practice and HSE HSG179 govern pool water treatment and operator competence, but the file found no pre-opening test frequency, record-retention wording or enforcement case, and none of it bears on chemical stock levels.
justifications.c5: A 'Facilities & Pool Plant Manager (Multi-Site)' advert (£30–35k) evidences a role responsible for dosing systems, but not budget authority; chemicals are bought by council tender.
justifications.c6: Chemical distributors deliver to pools (Monarch/Brenntag, Univar, Pool Pro, Woburn) and already run telemetry VMI elsewhere (Univar Remote Sentry, CGK auto-ordering), and pool dosing-equipment makers sell level-sensing lances; UK pool-specific distributor telemetry is not shown.
justifications.c7: Level sensing is built into current pool dosing kit: ProMinent suction lance with continuous level and DULCOnneX warning/error thresholds (search-confirmed), SEKO, Dinotec, Fluidra, Grundfos, Hanna cloud, plus generic IBC radar monitors; the only price is a low-quality pages.dev page, and the retrofit gap is inference.
justifications.c8: IBC-rated ultrasonic, submersible and external radar sensors exist (Flowline, E+H FWR30, DULCOlevel), but load-cell and LTE-M prices were not searched, and the hypochlorite/acid plant room is a corrosive environment.
justifications.c9: Chemical consumption and resupply recur and distributors monetise VMI telemetry, but there is no record-keeping duty tied to stock, and subscription pricing comes only from a single low-quality page (£30/mo).
justifications.c10: PWTAG news (search-confirmed), council notices (Hartlepool, Brighton & Hove) and local press (York, Blackpool, Bridlington) document chemical-related closures, but nearly all concern the 2022 national shortage, which a level sensor would not fix.

weakest: The specific failure is unevidenced and already solved: no UK pool closure from a drum running dry was found, and current dosing controllers (ProMinent, SEKO, Fluidra, Dinotec) already include level-sensing lances with cloud alarms.
